+## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic
+Pisot" AND "causal"`, `"Bertrand numeration" AND "sliding block"`,
+`"finite delay" AND "beta-expansion"`, and the exact Bassino title.  The
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 with `cache-control: private, no-store` through the
+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.

+## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic
+Pisot" AND "causal"`, `"Bertrand numeration" AND "sliding block"`,
+`"finite delay" AND "beta-expansion"`, and the exact Bassino title.  The
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 with `cache-control: private, no-store` through the
+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.

+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.

+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+

+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and

+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.

+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.

Furthermore, if additionally \\(\\mathbb{Q}(\\beta)\\) is not totally real, then \\(\\gamma(\\beta)\\) is irrational, so in particular, \\(\\gamma(\\beta)<1\\).\n\nAs usual, a Pisot number is a real algebraic integer which is greater than \\(1\\) and which has all Galois conjugates (different from itself) inside the open unit disc. A Pisot unit is a Pisot number which is a unit of the ring of integers of the number field it generates. Finally, \\(\\beta\\) is said to have property (F) if every \\(x\\in\\mathbb Z[1/\\beta] \\cap [0,1)\\) has a finite \\(\\beta\\)-expansion.\n\nThis is in partial contrast to quadratic \\(\\beta\\), where \\(\\gamma(\\beta)\\) is positive if and only if \\(\\beta\\) is a Pisot unit satisfying (F), but in that case, \\(\\gamma(\\beta)=1\\) always holds, which follows from work of \\textit{S. Up to a holomorphic change of coordinates, they can be expressed in the form\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned} \\textstyle{P(z}&\\textstyle{,w)}=\\textstyle{\\bigl(p(z),q(z,w)\\bigr)}\\\\\n&=\\textstyle{\\bigl(z-z^2+az^3+O(z^4),}\\\\\n&\\textstyle{\\qquad w+w^2+bz^2+b_{03}w^3+b_{30}z^3+O(\\|(z,w)\\|^4)\\bigr).} \\end{aligned}\n\\]\nA parabolic domain for \\(P\\) is a domain \\(U\\subset\\mathbb{C}^2\\) with \\(O\\in\\partial U\\) such that \\(P(U)\\subseteq U\\) and all orbits of \\(P\\) inside~\\(U\\) converge to the origin. If the orbits converge to~\\(O\\) tangentially to some direction~\\(v\\ne O\\), we say that \\(U\\) is tangent to~\\(v\\); otherwise, \\(U\\) is a parabolic spiral domain.\n\nThanks to the work of \\textit{M. Hakim} [Publ. Mat., Barc. 38, No. 2, 479--499 (1994; Zbl 0832.58031); Duke Math. J. 92, No. 2, 403--428 (1998; Zbl 0952.32012)] and \\textit{L. Vivas} [Indiana Univ. Math. On the other hand, if \\(b\\in(1/4,+\\infty)\\) the authors prove that \\(P\\) has a parabolic spiral domain.\n\nFor this reason, they focus their attention to the case \\(b\\in(1/4,+\\infty)\\), where they find a parabolic implosion structure that they then exploit to produce many examples of new phenomena. More precisely, the main theorem of this paper is the following. Assume that \\(b\\in(1/4,+\\infty)\\), put \\(c=\\frac{1}{2}\\sqrt{4b-1}>0\\), \\(\\alpha_0=e^{\\pi/c}>1\\) and assume that \\(\\beta_0=(b_{03}-a)(\\alpha_0-1)\\in\\mathbb{R}\\). Assume moreover that there exists a strictly increasing sequence \\((n_k)\\subset\\mathbb{N}^*\\) such that the sequence \\(\\sigma_k=n_{k+1}-\\alpha_0n_k-\\beta_0\\log n_k\\) is bounded. Then there exists a map \\(\\mathcal{L}\\) (a generalization of the Lavaurs map of parabolic implosion in one variable), depending only on the coefficients of the quadratic and cubic parts of~\\(P\\) and on the Fatou coordinates of \\(p\\) and of \\(q_0=q(0,\\cdot)\\), such that\n\\[\nP^{n_{k+1}-n_k}\\bigl(p^{n_k}(z),w\\bigr)=\\bigl(0,\\mathcal{L}(\\sigma_k;z,w)\\bigr)+o(1)\n\\]\nas \\(k\\to+\\infty\\). +## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic
+Pisot" AND "causal"`, `"Bertrand numeration" AND "sliding block"`,
+`"finite delay" AND "beta-expansion"`, and the exact Bassino title.  The
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 with `cache-control: private, no-store` through the
+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.

+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+

+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.

+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.

+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found

+or overlap-threshold predecessor.

+classification remains unproved.

+## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic
+Pisot" AND "causal"`, `"Bertrand numeration" AND "sliding block"`,
+`"finite delay" AND "beta-expansion"`, and the exact Bassino title.  The
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 with `cache-control: private, no-store` through the
+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.
+

+rank Pisot` returned no zbMATH record.  These negative results have the same
+query-language limitation as the other database searches and are not treated
+as proof of bibliographic nonexistence.

+## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic
+Pisot" AND "causal"`, `"Bertrand numeration" AND "sliding block"`,
+`"finite delay" AND "beta-expansion"`, and the exact Bassino title.  The
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 with `cache-control: private, no-store` through the
+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.

+## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic
+Pisot" AND "causal"`, `"Bertrand numeration" AND "sliding block"`,
+`"finite delay" AND "beta-expansion"`, and the exact Bassino title.  The
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 with `cache-control: private, no-store` through the
+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.
+

+## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic

+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.

+rank Pisot` returned no zbMATH record.  These negative results have the same
+query-language limitation as the other database searches and are not treated

+## Independent refresh for the cubic upgrade and named nearest work
+
+Checked: 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for `"cyclic language rank"`, `"cubic
+Pisot" AND "causal"`, `"Bertrand numeration" AND "sliding block"`,
+`"finite delay" AND "beta-expansion"`, and the exact Bassino title.  The
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 with `cache-control: private, no-store` through the
+LGA/Singapore Varnish route.  This is an API availability failure, not a
+zero-result search.  Google Scholar title/mechanism searches and Crossref
+bibliographic searches were therefore used as independent discovery checks.
+
+Crossref confirmed the following nearest-work records and DOI metadata:
+
+- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, *Numeration Systems on a Regular Language*,
+  Theory Comput. Systems **34** (2001), 27--44,
+  DOI `10.1007/s002240010014`.  Its published abstract introduces abstract
+  numeration by ordering an arbitrary infinite regular language and studies
+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are
+  published input, not a novelty claim.
+
+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.
+
+The zbMATH Open API supplied the MathSciNet-style subject-index check.  Exact
+title searches returned Lecomte--Rigo as Zbl `0969.68095`,
+Bruyere--Hansel as Zbl `0957.11015`, and Bassino as Zbl `1152.11342`.
+The Bassino query also returned Akiyama's *Cubic Pisot units with finite beta
+expansions* (Zbl `1001.11038`) and the established periodic-expansion
+literature.  Searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse` and `cyclic language
+rank Pisot` returned no zbMATH record.  These negative results have the same
+query-language limitation as the other database searches and are not treated
+as proof of bibliographic nonexistence.

The manuscript is now referee-safer, but I did not obtain the cubic theorem needed for a genuine tier upgrade. I stopped at the upgrade gate rather than convert strong finite evidence into an unproved theorem.

**(a) Prior Art**

The independent audit is recorded in [literature_check.md](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_sharp_three_window_threshold_fibonacci_conjugacy_dcds/artifacts/literature_check.md:208).

- Lecomte–Rigo and Bruyère–Hansel were already cited. I rewrote the introduction to state plainly that they supply genealogically ordered regular-language numeration, Bertrand systems, and recognizability, but not fixed-length cyclic reduction modulo \(Q_m\) or its overlap threshold.
- I added their DOIs and added Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`, in [bibliography.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_sharp_three_window_threshold_fibonacci_conjugacy_dcds/sections/bibliography.tex:18).
- Bassino already computes expansions of one for cubic Pisot numbers. Consequently, the candidate family’s Pisot/simple-Parry data are published input, not a contribution.
- Crossref, Google Scholar, zbMATH Open, and citation trails found no predecessor for the specific cyclic-modulo-\(Q_m\) collision-depth problem. zbMATH identifiers include Lecomte–Rigo `0969.68095`, Bruyère–Hansel `0957.11015`, and Bassino `1152.11342`.
- The arXiv Atom API returned HTTP 429 through its Singapore/LGA Varnish route. The audit records this as an availability failure, not as a zero-result search or proof of novelty.

**(b) Weakest Link**

I removed `lem:negative-two-window-bounded-carry`; its asserted “exhaustive table” did not contain an invariant or an exhaustive branch proof.

[05b_quadratic_pisot_extension.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_sharp_three_window_threshold_fibonacci_conjugacy_dcds/sections/05b_quadratic_pisot_extension.tex:775) now states the exact proved result:

\[
\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)=3\quad(\beta'>0,\ m\ge3),\qquad
\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,3)=2\quad(\beta'<0),
\]

and, for \(\beta'<0,\ m\ge4\),

\[
2\le\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)\le m.
\]

The negative \(m=3\) equality now has a complete proof from the previously established exhaustive triple list. The missing parameter-uniform two-window carry classification is an explicit open interface. The abstract, introduction, higher-degree section, and discussion were corrected consistently.

**(c) Upgrade Target**

Status: **attempted, out of reach with the present tools**.

Exact searches support
\(C_{n,r,r-1}=\{\pm E_{n,r}\}\) and \(C_{n,r,r}=\varnothing\) for every admissible \(r\) when \(4\le n\le6\), but finite enumeration is not a proof.

The missing input is specifically an all-\(n\), all-\(r\) classification that:

- rules out second-window carries \(\pm1\) using both complete weighted equations;
- proves the exact zero-carry deletion/lifting correspondence;
- handles a zero first coordinate after deletion;
- proves exhaustion and the unique extremal path recursively.

No different nearby theorem of comparable specialist value was both novel and provable from the current machinery. I therefore did not add the cubic family or claim unbounded cubic causal length.

**(d) Integrated Result**

No new cubic theorem was integrated. The only strengthened proof-level statement is the rigorous negative-chamber aperture-three causal optimum; larger apertures are explicitly bounded rather than falsely classified. No verifier was expanded merely to turn finite evidence into a theorem.

+  finite-automaton recognizability.  It supplies the ordered-language stage,
+  not cyclic reduction modulo a fixed-length language count or overlap
+  injectivity.
+- V. Bruyere and G. Hansel, *Bertrand numeration systems and
+  recognizability*, Theoret. Comput. Sci. **181** (1997), 17--43,
+  DOI `10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5`.  Its 26-item Crossref reference trail
+  includes Bertrand-Mathis, Parry, Frougny, Cobham, Shallit, and the classical
+  automata/linear-numeration literature.  It concerns Bertrand systems and
+  recognizable sets, not the manuscript's rank-modulo-`Q_m` sliding map.
+- F. Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, LATIN 2002,
+  pp. 141--152, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`.  The abstract states that the
+  expansion of one is computed for every cubic Pisot number and that cubic
+  simple beta-numbers are Pisot.  Its references include Akiyama, Boyd,
+  Frougny--Solomyak, Hollander, Parry, Schmidt, and Solomyak.  Consequently,
+  the Pisot/simple-Parry expansion data for the candidate cubic family are

+Exact Google Scholar searches for `"cyclic language rank" Pisot` and for the
+polynomial string `"x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n"` returned no matching scholarly
+title.  The broader search `"cubic Pisot" "sliding block"` returned work on
+beta-shifts/S-gap shifts and general automata material, not a cyclic
+language-rank fold.  Crossref searches for `cubic Pisot causal inverse`,
+`finite delay sliding block beta expansion`, and the exact polynomial found
+Bassino and established beta-expansion/arithmetic papers but no causal-depth
+or overlap-threshold predecessor.
+
+The defensible novelty boundary is therefore narrow.  Ordered regular-
+language numeration, Bertrand recognizability, cubic Pisot expansions, and
+simple-Parry admissibility are prior art.  The only potentially new cubic
+statement is the parameter-uniform modulus-`Q_m` collision-depth theorem.
+That statement is not integrated because its required all-parameter carry
+classification remains unproved.

**(a) Prior Art**

The independent audit is recorded in [literature_check.md](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_sharp_three_window_threshold_fibonacci_conjugacy_dcds/artifacts/literature_check.md:208).

- Lecomte–Rigo and Bruyère–Hansel were already cited. I rewrote the introduction to state plainly that they supply genealogically ordered regular-language numeration, Bertrand systems, and recognizability, but not fixed-length cyclic reduction modulo \(Q_m\) or its overlap threshold.
- I added their DOIs and added Bassino, *Beta-Expansions for Cubic Pisot Numbers*, DOI `10.1007/3-540-45995-2_17`, in [bibliography.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_sharp_three_window_threshold_fibonacci_conjugacy_dcds/sections/bibliography.tex:18).
- Bassino already computes expansions of one for cubic Pisot numbers. Consequently, the candidate family’s Pisot/simple-Parry data are published input, not a contribution.
- Crossref, Google Scholar, zbMATH Open, and citation trails found no predecessor for the specific cyclic-modulo-\(Q_m\) collision-depth problem. zbMATH identifiers include Lecomte–Rigo `0969.68095`, Bruyère–Hansel `0957.11015`, and Bassino `1152.11342`.
